وحدة ara::core — Adaptive Platform Core

المواصفة: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf (R25-11) · 1237 سجل API

function: 1060 type alias: 101 class: 34 struct: 26 variable: 13 enumeration: 3

دليل المستخدم مولَّد بالذكاء الاصطناعي / AI generated

وصف مولد تلقائياً، مشتق من حيث المحتوى من وثائق AUTOSAR R25-11 المشار إليها (مواصفة SWS والوثائق المعيارية المصاحبة) — وليس نصاً رسمياً لـ AUTOSAR. العبارات المعلّمة بأنها تفسير هي استنتاجات من المصادر.

Rolle & Verwendungszweck

Das Modul ara::core stellt das fundamentale Basis- und Laufzeitfundament der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform dar. Es definiert den gemeinsamen Standard für Datentypen, Fehlerbehandlungsmuster, asynchrone Kontrollflüsse und Lebenszyklusfunktionen über alle Functional Clusters sowie für anwendungsspezifischen Adaptive-Code hinweg [SWS_CORE_00001]. Um in sicherheitskritischen automobilen Steuergeräten deterministisches Verhalten zu garantieren, ersetzt ara::core traditionelle C++-Mechanismen wie unkontrollierte Exception-Weitergabe oder nicht echtzeitfähige Standard-Allokatoren durch explizite Typverträge.

Die Kernaufgaben von ara::core umfassen:

  • Einheitliches Fehlermodell: Bereitstellung von ara::core::Result<T, E> und ara::core::ErrorCode zur expliziten, typsicheren und ausnahmelosen Rückgabe von Fehlern im regulären Kontrollfluss.
  • Asynchronitätsmuster: Standardisierung von ara::core::Future und ara::core::Promise als konsistente Brücke für nebenläufige und verteilte Berechnungen in allen AUTOSAR-AP-Schnittstellen.
  • Port- und Instanzabstraktion: Bereitstellung des Typs ara::core::InstanceSpecifier, der logische Software-Architektur-Modellelemente auf konkrete Plattform- und Kommunikationskonfigurationen abbildet.
  • Lebenszyklus-Initialisierung: Zentraler Einstiegspunkt über Initialize() und Deinitialize() für das Hoch- und Herunterfahren der Adaptive Platform im Anwendungsprozess.
  • Automotive-fähige Hilfs- und Container-Typen: Typen wie Span, StringView, Optional und Variant zur ressourcenschonenden, kopierfreien Datenübergabe.

Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge

Alle öffentlichen ARA-Schnittstellen (AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive Applications) basieren zwingend auf den Typverträgen von ara::core. Die Spezifikation unterscheidet dabei funktionale Datenstrukturen, Identifikatoren und Fehlerbehandlungsprimitive:

  • Initialisierungsvertrag: Vor dem Aufruf jeglicher funktionaler ARA-APIs muss der Prozess ara::core::Initialize() aufrufen [SWS_CORE_00701]. Dieser Aufruf initialisiert interne Laufzeitstrukturen, Log-Sinks und abhängige Cluster. Vor Beendigung des Prozesses ist korrespondierend ara::core::Deinitialize() aufzurufen [SWS_CORE_00801].
  • Result- und Fehlervertrag: Operationen, die fehlschlagen können, liefern ein ara::core::Result<T, E> zurück [SWS_CORE_00733]. Ein Result kapselt entweder den gewünschten Wert vom Typ T oder einen ara::core::ErrorCode [SWS_CORE_00763]. Jeder ErrorCode referenziert eine konkrete ErrorDomain mit eindeutiger 64-Bit-Kennung [SWS_CORE_00767], wodurch Fehlernummern clusterübergreifend kollisionsfrei interpretiert werden.
  • Asynchroner Vertrag: Asynchrone Schnittstellen liefern ein ara::core::Future<T, E> zurück [SWS_CORE_00736]. Aufrufer können synchron auf das Eintreffen warten (wait(), wait_for()) oder über GetResult() das finale Result<T, E> abholen, ohne dass C++-Standardausnahmen geworfen werden.
  • Instanzbindung: Der ara::core::InstanceSpecifier kapselt einen qualifizierten Manifest-Pfad (z. B. /Executable/PortPrototype) als eindeutigen Schlüssel zur Konfigurationsauflösung [SWS_CORE_08001].
  • Forwarding-Header: Der Namensraum ara ist für AUTOSAR reserviert. Um Compile-Zeiten zu optimieren und modulare Abhängigkeiten zu trennen, stellt jeder Cluster Forwarding-Header <fc>_fwd.h bereit.

Interaktionsfluss

Der Lebenszyklus einer Adaptive Application beginnt typischerweise mit dem Aufruf von Initialize(). Anschließend werden funktionale Cluster wie ara::com, ara::exec oder ara::diag verwendet, wobei asynchrone Schnittstellen durch das Zusammenspiel von Promise und Future synchronisiert werden. Vor dem Prozessende stellt Deinitialize() den geordneten Rückbau aller Cluster-Ressourcen sicher.

Interaktionsdiagramm: Initialisierung des Basissystems über Initialize(), asynchroner Arbeitsfluss über Promise und Future, Fehlerrückgabe via Result/ErrorCode und geordneter Shutdown über Deinitialize(). Quellen: [SWS_CORE_00701], [SWS_CORE_00801], [SWS_CORE_00733] und [SWS_CORE_00736].

Konfiguration & Fehlerbehandlung

Für Fehler und Ausnahmezustände etabliert ara::core eine strikte Zwei-Klassen-Architektur:

  • Behebbare Fehler (Recoverable Errors): Diese spiegeln erwartbare Fehlerszenarien wider (z. B. Timeout, temporäre Nichtverfügbarkeit eines Dienstes oder ungültige Nutzereingaben). Sie werden über Result<T, E> an den Aufrufer übergeben und müssen von der Fachlogik ausgewertet und behandelt werden [SWS_CORE_00021].
  • Unbehebbare Regelverletzungen (Violations): Violations resultieren aus verletzten Vor- oder Nachbedingungen, Programmierfehlern oder korrumpierten Speicherzuständen des Frameworks. Bei einer Violation bricht das System die Ausführung sofort und unumkehrbar über ara::core::Abort() ab [SWS_CORE_00090] [SWS_CORE_12404]. Parallel ankommende Threads blockieren während Abort() [SWS_CORE_12407], um unkontrollierte Kaskadeneffekte zu unterbinden.

Zur einheitlichen Diagnose und Rückverfolgbarkeit definiert ara::core standardisierte Logging-Kontext-IDs je Funktionscluster, u. a. #COR für Core, #COM für Communication Management, #EXE für Execution Management und #DIA für Diagnostics [SWS_CORE_00055] [SWS_CORE_90024].

Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

ERWARTETES AUSGABEFORMAT:
Antworte AUSSCHLIESSLICH im validen JSON-Format gemäß folgendem Schema:
Erwartete Ausgabe: JSON-Datei mit demselben Namen wie dieser Auftrag,
Endung .out.json statt .json, im selben Verzeichnis. Aufbau:
{"ergebnisse": [{
  "fragment":  "<wie im Auftrag>",
  "html":      "<vollständiges <div class=\"ai …\">-Fragment, deutsch>",
  "diagramme": {"<pfad relativ zu _src>": "<Quelltext .dot | .seq.json>"},
  "trace": {"prompt": "<der bearbeitete Auftragstext>",
            "modell": "<verwendetes Modell>",
            "wissen":   [{"aussage": "...", "quelle": "<dok-id>", "fundstelle": "..."}],
            "annahmen": [{"annahme": "...", "begruendung": "..."}],
            "transkript": "<Denkprozess/Begründungsgang dieses Laufs>",
            "diagramme": {"<pfad>": {"entscheidung": "...", "annahmen": [...],
                                     "transkript": "..."}}}}]}
Alle Vorgaben aus policy und richtlinien sind bindend (Belegpflicht,
Annahmen-Budget, Diagramm-Kriterien, ai-note, deutsche Sprache).

        "html": "<h3 class=\"recname\"><span class=\"kind\">function</span> ErrorOr <span class=\"sws\"><a href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00764\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf)\">[SWS_CORE_00764]</a></span> <span class=\"ups\">Upstream: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00130\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00130</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">template &lt;typename G&gt; <a href=\"#class-decl\">E</a> ErrorOr (G &amp;&amp;defaultError) &amp;&amp;noexcept(<a class=\"cppref\" href=\"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/is_move_constructible\" title=\"cppreference.com (C++17)\">std::is_nothrow_move_ constructible</a>&lt; <a href=\"#class-decl\">E</a> &gt;::value &amp;&amp;<a class=\"cppref\" href=\"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/is_constructible\" title=\"cppreference.com (C++17)\">std::is_nothrow_constructible</a>&lt; <a href=\"#class-decl\">E</a>, G &amp;&amp; &gt;::value);</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Return the contained error or the given default error. If *this contains an error, it is std:: move’d into the return value. Otherwise, the specified default error is returned, static_cast’d to E</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n\n"

    "SWS_CORE_00767": [
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<h3 class=\"recname\"><span class=\"kind\">function</span> Resolve <span class=\"sws\"><a href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00767\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf)\">[SWS_CORE_00767]</a></span> <span class=\"ups\">Upstream: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00130\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00130</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">template &lt;typename F&gt; <a href=\"#class-decl\">T</a> Resolve (F &amp;&amp;f) const;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Return the contained value or return the result of a function call.</p><p>If *this contains a value, it is returned. Otherwise, the specified callable is invoked and its return value which is to be compatible to type T is returned from this function.</p><p>The Callable is expected to be compatible to this interface: T f(const E&amp;);</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n\n"
      },
      {

    "SWS_CORE_00768": [
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<h3 class=\"recname\"><span class=\"kind\">function</span> Bind <span class=\"sws\"><a href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00768\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf)\">[SWS_CORE_00768]</a></span> <span class=\"ups\">Upstream: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00130\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00130</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">template &lt;typename F&gt; auto Bind (F &amp;&amp;f) const -&gt; &lt;see below&gt;;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Apply the given Callable to the value of this instance, and return a new <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html\">ara::core</a>:: Result with the result of the call.</p><p>The Callable is expected to be compatible to one of these two interfaces: • Result&lt;XXX, E&gt; f(const T&amp;); • &lt;ARTechTerm{XXX f(const T&amp;);}&gt; • &lt;ARNewline{}&gt; • &lt;ARNewline{}&gt; • &lt;ARTechTerm{Callable}&gt; • Result&lt;XXX&gt; or a XXX directly, where XXX can be any type that is suitable for use by <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>.</p><p>The return type of this function is decltype(f(Value())) for a template argument F that returns a <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a> type, and it is Result&lt;decltype(f(Value())), E&gt; for a template argument F that does not return a <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a> type.</p><p>If this instance does not contain a value, a new Result&lt;XXX, E&gt; is still created and returned, with the original error contents of this instance being copied into the new instance.}&gt;}</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n\n"
      },
      {

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P1_03",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 1,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "•\nAdd spec items for error handling\ndefinitions\n•\nAdd specifications for\nScaleLinearAndTexttable, taken over\nfrom\nSWS_CommunicationManagement\n•\nRefine scope of ara::core::Initialize\n•\nAdapt some APIs to C++14's\nenhanced capabilities\n•\nAlign Span with std::span from the\nC++20 standard\n•\nReduce requirements imposed on\nhandling Violations\n•\nRename document into Adaptive\nPlatform Core"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P1_04",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",

    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P2_05",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 2,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P2_06",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 2,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "•\nAdd specifications about Explicit\nOperation Abortion\n•\nAdd specification about reserved\nsymbol prefixes\n•\nAdd specification of class\nSteadyClock\n•\nAdd section about async signal\nsafety of ARA APIs\n•\nExtend error domain scope with\nvendor-defined error domains\n•\nAdd specifications about defining\nown error domains\n•\nVarious extensions and fixes to the\nC++ data types\n•\nIncorporate contents of\nSWS_General\n•\nRename document into Adaptive\nCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P2_07",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 2,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "•\nRework error handling definitions\n•\nAdd specifications of BasicString and\nByte, and add overloads and\ntemplate specializations for\nErrorCode, Result, Future, and\nPromise\n•\nAdd bits about validity of\nInstanceSpecifier arguments, and\nrework the specification of its\nconstruction mechanism\n•\nRework ErrorCode to get rid of User\nMessage and make\nSupportDataType\nimplementation-defined\n•\nReplace PosixErrorDomain with\nCoreErrorDomain\n•\nRename FutureErrorDomain\naccessor function\n•\nChanged Document Status from\nFinal to published"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P8_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n1 Introduction\nThis document defines basic requirements that apply to all Functional Clusters of the\nAdaptive Platform.\nTo aid in this, it also defines functionality that applies to the entire framework, including\na set of common data types used by multiple Functional Clusters as part of their public\ninterfaces.\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to Adaptive Core\nthat are not included in the [1, AUTOSAR glossary]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P8_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Immediate abortion of an API call, which is initiated by calling\nara::core::Abort\n, usually as a consequence of the detection\nof a\nViolation\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P8_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\n[1] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_TR_Glossary\n[2] Specification of Operating System Interface\nAUTOSAR_SWS_OperatingSystemInterface\n[3] Functional Cluster Shortnames\nAUTOSAR_TR_FunctionalClusterShortnames\n[4] ISO/IEC 14882:2014, Information technology  Programming languages  C++\nhttp://www.iso.org\n[5] ValueOrError and ValueOrNone types\nhttp://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2018/p0786r1.pdf\n[6] Standard for Information TechnologyPortable Operating System Interface\n(POSIX(R)) Base Specifications, Issue 7\nhttp://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/\n[7] Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR_SWS_ExecutionManagement\n8 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P9_18",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 9,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[8] Explanation of ara::com API\nAUTOSAR_EXP_ARAComAPI\n[9] N4659: Working Draft, Standard for ProgrammingLanguage C++\nhttp://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2017/n4659.pdf\n[10] N4820: Working Draft, Standard for Programming Language C++\nhttp://www.open-std.org/JTC1/SC22/WG21/docs/papers/2019/n4820.pdf\n[11] N3857: Improvements to std::future<T> and Related APIs\nhttps://isocpp.org/files/papers/N3857.pdf\n9 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P10_19",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 10,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\n•\nThe specification of some data types (Array, Map, Optional, String, StringView,\nVariant) mentions supporting constructs, but lacks a precise scope definition of\nthis term.\n•\nThe specification of some data types (Map, Vector, String) is lacking a compre-\nhensive definition of memory allocation behavior; it currently only describes it as\nimplementation-defined.\n•\nChapter 7.2 (Functional Specification) describes some behavior informally that\nshould rather be given as specification items.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nNo restrictions to applicability.\n5 Dependencies to other modules\nThis Functional Cluster only depends on [2], in particular the C++ standard library.\n10 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P11_20",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_90001",

      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n6 Requirements Tracing\nThe following tables reference the requirements specified in <CITA-\nTIONS_OF_CONTRIBUTED_DOCUMENTS> and links to the fulfillment of these.\nPlease note that if column Satisfied by is empty for a specific requirement this means\nthat this requirement is not fulfilled by this document."

    {

      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_08001",

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P23_73",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_90001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7 Requirements Specification\n7.1 General requirements for all Functional Clusters\nThe goal of this section is to define a common set of basic requirements that apply\nto all Functional Clusters of the Adaptive Platform. It adds a common part to the\nspecifications and it needs to be respected by platform vendors.\n[SWS_CORE_90001] Include folder structure\n⌈\nAll #include directives in header files\nthat refer to ARA libraries shall be written in the form\n#include \"ara/fc/header.h\"\nwith ara as the first path element, fc being the remaining directory path of the imple-\nmentation's\ninstalled\nheader file, starting with the Functional Cluster short name, and\nheader.h being the filename of the header file.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00116, RS_AP_00111)\nThe Functional Cluster short names are defined in [3].\nExample: Execution Management (short name exec) provides class\nExecution-\nClient\n, which can be accessed with:\n#include \"ara/exec/execution_client.h\"\nThe \"...\" form of #include statements shall be used, due to the recommendation given\nin [4, the C++14 standard] section 16.2.7.\n[SWS_CORE_90002] Prevent multiple inclusion of header file\n⌈\nAll public header\nfiles shall prevent multiple inclusion by using #include guards that are likely to be\nsystem-wide unique.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00111)\nWhile uniqueness can generally not be guaranteed, the likelihood of collisions can be\ndecreased with a naming scheme that is regular and results in long symbol names.\nThe following #include guard naming scheme should be used by implementations for\nall header files that cover symbols within the\nara\nnamespace or a sub-namespace\ntherein:\nARA_<PATH>_H_\nwhere <PATH> is the relative path name of the header file within the location of the\nimplementation's\ninstalled\nheader files, starting with the Functional Cluster name (and\nomitting the file extension), and with all components of <PATH> separated by under-\nscore (\"_\") characters and containing only upper-case characters of the ASCII charac-\nter set.\nExample: The header file included with\n#include \"ara/log/logger.h\"\nshould\nuse the #include guard symbol\nARA_LOG_LOGGER_H_\n.\n23 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P24_74",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_90003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 24,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_90003]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\nC/C++ symbols that start with\nARA\nare reserved for\nuse by AUTOSAR.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00111)\nThe Adaptive Platform generally avoids the use of C/C++ preprocessor macros. How-\never, in case macros are introduced at some later point in time, any such macro will\nstart with the prefix\nARA\n. Platform vendors should thus not define any symbols (both\nmacros and C/C++ ones) with this prefix, lest they conflict with such future additions to\nthe standard.\n[SWS_CORE_90004]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nImplementation-defined declaration classifiers\n⌈\nAll\nAPIs shall be implemented with the exact same declaration classifiers that are speci-\nfied, except for\ninline\nand\nfriend\n, which may be added as necessary.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00111)\nNote: The order of declarations may be freely chosen.\n[4, The C++14 standard] defines in chapter 7.1 [dcl.spec] the specifiers that can be\nused in a declaration; these include, for instance,\nstatic\n,\nvirtual\n,\nconstexpr\n,\ninline\nand\nfriend\n. An implementation that uses a different set of specifiers in its\ndeclaration of a specified API may be incompatible to the standard, or may allow non-\nstandardized usage of that API, leading to portability concerns.\n7.1.1 Initialize/Deinitialize\nara::core::Initialize\nallows a central initialization of all included shared li-\nbraries of the ARA framework. This could include static initializers or the setup of\ndaemon links (details are up to the platform vendor).\nThe general advice for application developers is to call\nara::core::Initialize\nright at the entry point of the application.\n[SWS_CORE_90020]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\nIf functionality is called that depends on prior initial-\nization via\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Initialize\nhas not been\ncalled, the Functional Cluster implementation shall treat this as a\nViolation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00111)\nThe rationale to treat this as a\nViolation\nis that it cannot be handled by the caller of\nthe API at the point in time where the error is detected. Aborting execution is the only\nway to signal this kind of systematic error and prevent later failures.\n24 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P25_75",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00020",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 25,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2 Functional Specification\nThis section describes the concepts that are introduced with this Functional Cluster.\nParticular emphasis is put on error handling.\n7.2.1 Error handling\n7.2.1.1 Types of unsuccessful operations\nDuring execution of an implementation of Adaptive Platform APIs, different abnormal\nconditions might be detected and need to be handled and/or reported. Based on\ntheir nature, the following types of unsuccessful operations are distinguished within\nthe Adaptive Platform:\n[SWS_CORE_00020]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of an Error\n⌈\nAn\nError\nis the inability of\nan assumed-bug-free API function to fulfill its specified purpose; it is often a conse-\nquence of invalid and/or unexpected (i.e. possibly valid, but received in unexpected\ncircumstances) input data. An\nError\nis recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00021]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Violation\n⌈\nA\nViolation\nis the con-\nsequence of failed pre- or post-conditions of internal state of the application framework.\nThey are the Adaptive Platform's analog to a failed assertion. A\nViolation\nis non-\nrecoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00022]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Corruption\n⌈\nA\nCorruption\nis the\nconsequence of the corruption of a system resource, e.g. stack or heap overflow, or a\nhardware memory flaw (including even, for instance, a detected bit flip). A\nCorrup-\ntion\nis non-recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00023]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Failed Default Allocation\n⌈\nA\nFailed Default Allocation\nis the inability of the framework's default memory\nallocation mechanism to satisfy an allocation request. A\nFailed Default Alloca-\ntion\nis non-recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nIt is expected that a\nViolation\nor\nCorruption\nmight occur during development of\nthe framework, when new features are just coming together, but will not be experienced\nby a user (i.e. an application developer), unless there is something seriously wrong in\nthe system's environment (e.g. faulty hardware:\nCorruption\n), or basic assumptions\nabout resource requirements are violated (\nViolation\n), or possibly the user runs the\nframework in a configuration that is not supported by its vendor (\nViolation\n).\n7.2.1.2 Traditional error handling in C and C++\nThe C language largely relies on error codes for any kind of error handling. While it\nalso has the\nsetjmp\n/\nlongjmp\nfacility for performing non-local gotos, its use for error\n25 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P26_76",
      "source_element": null,

      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nhandling is not widespread, mostly due to the difficulty of reliably avoiding resource\nleaks.\nError codes in C come in several flavors:\n•\nreturn values\n•\nout parameters\n•\nerror singletons (e.g.\nerrno\n)\nTypically, these error codes in C are plain\nint\nvariables, making them a very low-level\nfacility without any type safety.\nC++ inherited these approaches to error handling from C (not least due to the inher-\nitance of the C standard library as part of the C++ standard), but it also introduced\nexceptions as an alternative means of error propagation. There are many advantages\nof using exceptions for error propagation, which is why the C++ standard library gen-\nerally relies on them for error propagation.\nNotwithstanding the advantages of exceptions, error codes are still in widespread use\nin C++, even within the standard library. Some of that can be explained with concerns\nabout binary compatibility with C, but many new libraries still prefer error codes to\nexceptions. Reasons for that include:\n•\nwith exceptions, it can be difficult to reason about a program's control flow\n•\nexceptions have much higher runtime cost than error codes (either in general, or\nonly in the exception-thrown case)\nThe first of these reasons concerns both humans and code analysis tools. Because\nexceptions are, in effect, a kind of hidden control flow, a C++ function that seems to\ncontain only a single\nreturn\nstatement might in fact have many additional function\nreturns due to exceptions. That can make such a function hard to review for humans,\nbut also hard to analyze for static code analysis tools.\nThe second one is even more critical in the context of developing safety-critical soft-\nware. The specification of C++ exceptions pose significant problems for C++ compiler\nvendors that want their products be certified for development of safety-critical software.\nIn fact, ASIL-certified C++ compilers generally do not support exceptions at all. One\nparticular problem with exceptions is that exception handling, as specified for C++, im-\nplies the use of dynamic memory allocation, which generally has non-predictable or\neven unbounded execution time. This makes exceptions currently unsuitable for devel-\nopment of certain safety-critical software in the automotive industry.\n7.2.1.3 Handling of unsuccessful operations in the Adaptive Platform\nThe types of unsuccessful operations defined in section 7.2.1.1 (Types of unsuccessful\noperations) are to be treated in different ways.\n26 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P27_77",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_00002] Handling of Errors\n⌈\nAn\nError\nshall be returned from the func-\ntion as an instance of\nara::core::Result\nor\nara::core::Future\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00142, RS_AP_00139, RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_CORE_00003] Handling of Violations\n⌈\nIf a\nViolation\nis detected, then the\noperation shall be terminated by either:\n•\nthrowing an exception that is not a subclass of\nara::core::Exception\n•\nexplicitly terminating the process abnormally via a call to\nara::core::Abort\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00004] Handling of Corruptions\n⌈\nIf a\nCorruption\nis detected, it shall\nresult in unsuccessful process termination, in an implementation-defined way.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00142)\nNote: It can either be abnormal or normal unsuccessful termination, depending on the\nimplementation's ability to detect the\nCorruption\nand to react to it by cleaning up\nresources.\n[SWS_CORE_00005] Handling of failed default allocations\n⌈\nA \"failed default allo-\ncation\" shall be treated the same as a\nViolation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nNote: An error of a custom allocator is not subject to this definition.\n7.2.1.4 Facilities for Error Handling\nFor handling\nErrors\n, there are a number of data types defined that help in dealing\nwith them. These are described in the following subsections.\n7.2.1.4.1 ErrorCode\nAs its name implies,\nara::core::ErrorCode\nis a form of error code; however, it\nis a class type, loosely modeled on\nstd::error_code\n, and thus allows much more\nsophisticated handling of errors than the simple error codes as used in typical C APIs.\nIt always contains a low-level\nerror code value\nand a reference to an\nerror do-\nmain\n.\nThe\nerror code value\nis an enumeration, typically a scoped one. When stored into\na\nara::core::ErrorCode\n, it is type-erased into an integral type and thus handled\nsimilarly to a C-style error code. The\nerror domain\nreference defines the context for\nwhich the\nerror code value\nis applicable and thus provides some measure of type\nsafety.\nAn\nara::core::ErrorCode\nalso contains a\nsupport data value\n, which\ncan\nbe\ndefined by an implementation of the Adaptive Platform to give a vendor-specific addi-\ntional piece of data about the error.\n27 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P28_78",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10302",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_10302]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of ErrorCode\n⌈\nThe type\nara::core::-\nErrorCode\nprovides a class interface for storing an error condition. It shall contain\nthese properties:\n•\nerror code value: an integral representation of a low-level error code\n•\nerror domain: reference to the context for which the\nerror code value\nis applicable\n•\nsupport data value: an optional vendor-specific additional piece of data about the\nerror\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances are usually not created directly, but only via the\nforwarding form of the function\nara::core::Result::FromError\n.\nAn\nara::core::ErrorCode\nis not restricted to any known set of error domains.\nIts internal type erasure of the enumeration makes sure that it is a simple (i.e., non-\ntemplated) type which can contain arbitrary errors from arbitrary domains.\nHowever, comparison of two\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances only considers the\nerror code value\nand the\nerror domain\nreference; the\nsupport data value\nmember is not considered for checking equality. This is due to the way\nara::core:-\n:ErrorCode\ninstances are usually compared against a known set of errors for which\nto check:\n1\nErrorCode ec = ...\n2\nif (ec == MyEnum::some_error)\n3\n// ...\n4\nelse if (ec == AnotherEnum::another_error)\n5\n// ...\nEach of these comparisons will create a temporary\nara::core::ErrorCode\nobject\nfor the right-hand side of the comparison, and then compare\nec\nagainst that. Such au-\ntomatically created instances naturally do not contain any meaningful\nsupport data\nvalue\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10301]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nComparison of ara::core::ErrorCode instances\n⌈\nAny comparison of two\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances shall consider only the\nfollowing members:\n•\nerror code value\n•\nerror domain\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nThis frequent creation of temporary\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances is expected\nto be so fast as to induce no noticeable runtime cost. This is usually ensured by\nara::core::ErrorCode\nbeing a\nliteral type\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10300]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorCode type properties\n⌈\nClass\nara::core::-\nErrorCode\nshall be a\nliteral type\n, as defined in section 3.9-10 [basic.types] of [4, the\nC++14 standard].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n28 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P29_79",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10303",

      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2.1.4.2 ErrorDomain\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nis the abstract base class for concrete error domains\nthat are defined within Functional Clusters or even Adaptive Applications. This class is\nloosely based on\nstd::error_category\n, but differs significantly from it.\nAn error domain has an associated error code enumeration and an associated base\nexception type. Both these are usually defined in the same namespace as the\nara:-\n:core::ErrorDomain\nsubclass. For normalized access to these associated types,\ntype aliases with standardized names are defined within the\nara::core::Error-\nDomain\nsubclass. This makes the\nErrorDomain\nsubclass the root of all data about\nerrors.\n[SWS_CORE_10303]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of ErrorDomain\n⌈\nThe type\nara::-\ncore::ErrorDomain\ndefines a context for a set of error conditions.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nIdentity of error domains is defined in terms of unique identifiers. AUTOSAR-defined\nerror domains are given standardized identifiers; user-defined error domains are also\nrequired to define unique identifiers.\nThe\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nclass definition requires this unique identifier to be\nof unsigned 64 bit integer type (\nstd::uint64_t\n). The range of possible values is\nlarge enough to apply UUID-like generation patterns (for\nUID-64\n) even if typical UUIDs\nhave 128 bits and are thus larger than that. When a new error domain is created (ei-\nther an AUTOSAR defined or an user defined one) an according\nId\nshall be randomly\ngenerated, which represents this error domain. The uniqueness and standardization\nof such an\nId\nper error domain is mandatory, since the exchange of information on oc-\ncured errors between callee and caller (potentially located at different ECUs) is based\non this\nId\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10401]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nIdentity of ErrorDomains\n⌈\nTwo instances of\nara:-\n:core::ErrorDomain\nshall compare equal if and only if their unique identifiers are\nthe same.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nGiven this definition of identity of error domains, it usually makes sense to have only\none single instance of each\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nsubclass. While new in-\nstances of these subclasses can be created by calling their constructors, the rec-\nommended way to gain access to these subclasses is to call their global accessor\nfunctions. For instance, the error domain class\nara::core::FutureErrorDomain\nis referenced by calling\nara::core::GetFutureErrorDomain\n; within any process\nspace, this will always return a reference to the same global instance of this class.\nFor error domains that are modeled in ARXML (as\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n),\nthe C++ language binding will create a C++ class for each such\nApApplication-\nErrorDomain\n. This C++ class will be a subclass of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\n,\nand its name will follow a standard scheme.\nara::core\nhas two pre-defined error domains, called\nara::core::CoreErrorDo-\nmain\n(containing the set of errors returned by non-\nFuture\n/\nPromise\nfacilities from the\n29 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nara::core\nFunctional Cluster) and\nara::core::FutureErrorDomain\n(containing\nerrors equivalent to those defined by\nstd::future_errc\n).\nApplication programmers usually do not interact with class\nara::core::ErrorDo-\nmain\nor its subclasses directly; most access is done via\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\nAs\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nsubclasses are expected to be implicitly referred to\nfrom within constant (i.e. compile-time) expressions (typically involving\nara::core:-\n:ErrorCode\n), they are expected to be\nliteral types\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10400]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain type properties\n⌈\nClass\nara::core:-\n:ErrorDomain\nand all its subclasses shall be\nliteral types\n, as defined in section 3.9-10\n[basic.types] of [4, the C++14 standard].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.1.4.3 Result\nThe\nara::core::Result\ntype follows the\nValueOrError\nconcept from the C++\nproposal p0786 [5]. It either contains a value (of type\nValueType\n), or an error (of type\nErrorType\n). Both\nValueType\nand\nErrorType\nare template parameters of\nara:-\n:core::Result\n, and due to their templated nature, both value and error can be of\nany type. However,\nErrorType\nis defaulted to\nara::core::ErrorCode\n, and it is\nexpected that this assignment is kept throughout the Adaptive Platform.\nara::core::Result\nacts as a wrapper type that connects the exception-less API\napproach using\nara::core::ErrorCode\nwith C++ exceptions. As there is a di-\nrect mapping between\nara::core::ErrorCode\nand a domain-specific exception\ntype,\nara::core::Result\nallows to transform its embedded\nara::core::Er-\nrorCode\ninto the appropriate exception type, by calling\nara::core::Result::-\nValueOrThrow\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10600]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of ara::core::Result\n⌈\nThe type\nara::-\ncore::Result\nshall provide a means to handle both return values and errors from\nsynchronous function calls in an exception-less way, by providing an encapsulated\nreturn type which may be either:\n•\na value\nV\n, where\nV\nmay be any C++ type; or\n•\nan error\nE\n, where\nE\nmay be any C++ type; default is\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_00142, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_00119)\n7.2.1.4.4 Future and Promise\nara::core::Future\nand its companion class\nara::core::Promise\nare closely\nmodeled on\nstd::future\nand\nstd::promise\n, but have been adapted to interoper-\nate with\nara::core::Result\n. Similar to\nara::core::Result\ndescribed in section\n7.2.1.4.3, the class\nara::core::Future\neither contains a value, or an error (the\nFu-\n30 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nture\nfirst has to be in ready state, though). Class\nara::core::Promise\nhas been\nadapted in two aspects:\nstd::promise::set_exception\nhas been removed, and\nara::core::Promise::SetError\nhas been introduced in its stead. For\nara::-\ncore::Future\n, there is a new member function\nara::core::Future::GetRe-\nsult\nthat is similar to\nara::core::Future::get\n, but never throws an exception\nand returns a\nara::core::Result\ninstead.\nThus,\nara::core::Future\nas return type allows the same dual approach to er-\nror handling as\nara::core::Result\n, in that it either works exception-based (with\nara::core::Future::get\n), or exception-free (with\nara::core::Future::Ge-\ntResult\n).\nara::core::Result\nis a type used for returning values or errors from a\nsynchronous\nfunction call, whereas\nara::core::Future\nis a type used for returning values or\nerrors from an\nasynchronous\nfunction call.\n[SWS_CORE_10800]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of ara::core::Future and\nara::core::Promise\n⌈\nThe types\nara::core::Future\nand\nara::core::Promise\nshall provide a means to handle both return values and errors from asynchronous\nfunction calls in an exception-less way. Together, they provide a means to store a value\ntype\nT\nor an error type\nE\nwhich may be asynchronously retrieved in a thread-safe\nmanner at a later point in time.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00138, RS_AP_00128)\n7.2.1.5 Duality of ErrorCode and exceptions\nBy using the classes listed above, all APIs of the Adaptive Platform can be used with ei-\nther an exception-based or an exception-less error handling workflow. However, no API\nfunction will ever treat an\nError\nby throwing an exception directly; it will always return\nan error code in the form of a\nara::core::Result\nor\nara::core::Future\nreturn\nvalue instead. It is then possible for the caller to transform the\nError\ninto an excep-\ntion, typically via the member function\nara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow\n.\nWhen working with a C++ compiler that does not support exceptions at all (or one\nthat has been configured to disable them with an option such as g++'s\n-fno-\nexceptions\n), all API functions still show the same behavior. What\ndoes\ndiffer then is\nthat\nara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow\nis not defined  this member function is\nonly defined when the compiler does support exceptions.\n7.2.1.6 Exception hierarchy\nThe Adaptive Platform defines a base exception type\nara::core::Exception\nfor all\nexceptions defined in the standard. This exception takes a\nara::core::ErrorCode\nobject as mandatory constructor argument, similar to the way\nstd::system_error\ntakes a\nstd::error_code\nargument for construction.\n31 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P32_82",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10999",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nBelow this exception base type, there is an additional layer of exception base types,\none for each error domain.\nFor error domains that are modeled in ARXML, the C++ language binding will gener-\nate an exception class in addition to the ErrorDomain subclass (which is described in\nsection 7.2.1.4.2). This exception class also conforms to a standard naming scheme:\n<shortname> of\nApApplicationErrorDomain\nplus Exception suffix (this makes\nit distinguishable from the\nErrorDomain\nsubclass itself). It is located in the same\nnamespace as the corresponding\nErrorDomain\nsubclass.\n7.2.1.7 Creating new error domains\nAny new software module with significant logical separation from all existing modules\nof the Adaptive Platform should define one or more own error domains.\nAn error domain consists of:\n•\nan error condition enumeration\n•\nan exception base class\n•\nan\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nsubclass\n•\na global\nErrorDomain\nsubclass accessor function\n•\na global\nMakeErrorCode\nfunction overload\nAll these are to reside not in the\nara::core\nnamespace, but in the target one.\n[SWS_CORE_10999]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nCustom error domain scope\n⌈\nThe\nara::core::-\nErrorDomain\nsubclass and the corresponding enumeration, exception base class,\nglobal accessor function, and the\nMakeErrorCode\noverload shall be defined in the\nsame namespace as the software module for which they are being specified.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00130)\nNote: This is to help making sure that the C++ ADL mechanism works as expected by\nother parts of this standard.\nAn error domain defined in the way specified in this section is suitable to be used for\nthe\nApApplicationErrorDomain\nmodel element.\nThroughout this section, the character sequence\n<SN>\nis a placeholder for the\nshort-\nname\nof the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n.\n7.2.1.7.1 Error condition enumeration\nThe error condition enumeration describes all known error conditions of the new soft-\nware module. It should be reasonably fine-grained to allow users to differentiate error\nconditions that they might want to handle in different ways.\n32 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },

      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_10900]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nError condition enumeration type\n⌈\nEach error do-\nmain shall define an error condition enum class with the base type\nara::core::-\nErrorDomain::CodeType\nthat holds all error conditions of that error domain.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10901]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nError condition enumeration naming\n⌈\nError domain\nerror condition enumerations shall follow the naming scheme\n<SN>Errc\n, where\n<SN>\nis the shortname of the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10902]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nError condition enumeration contents\n⌈\nError do-\nmain error condition enumerations shall not contain any values that indicate success.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10903]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nError condition enumeration numbers\n⌈\nError do-\nmain error condition enumerations shall keep the number 0 unassigned.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\n7.2.1.7.2 Exception base class\nAs a complement to the error condition enumeration, an exception base class for this\nerror domain also needs to be defined. This exception base class is used for the\ntransformation of an\nara::core::ErrorCode\nobject into an exception.\nAdditional exception types can be defined by the software module, but all these then\nderive from this base type.\n[SWS_CORE_10910]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain exception base type\n⌈\nEach error do-\nmain shall define an exception base type that is a subclass of\nara::core::Excep-\ntion\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10911]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain exception base type naming\n⌈\nAll er-\nror domain exception base types specified by [SWS_CORE_10910] shall follow the\nnaming scheme\n<SN>Exception\n, where\n<SN>\nis the shortname of the\nApApplica-\ntionErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10912]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain exception type hierarchy\n⌈\nAll addi-\ntional exception types defined by a software module shall have the exception base\ntype specified by [SWS_CORE_10910] as a base class.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.1.7.3 ErrorDomain subclass\nThen, a new class is created that derives from\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nand over-\nrides all the pure virtual member functions. In addition to that, it also needs to define\nin its scope a type alias called\nErrc\nfor the error condition enumeration, as well as\nanother type alias called\nException\nfor the exception base class for this new error\ndomain.\n33 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_10930]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass type\n⌈\nEach error domain\nshall define a class type that derives publicly from\nara::core::ErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10931]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass naming\n⌈\nAll subclasses of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nshall follow the naming scheme\n<SN>ErrorDomain\n,\nwhere\n<SN>\nis the shortname of the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10932]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass non-extensibility\n⌈\nAll sub-\nclasses of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nshall be\nfinal\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130, RS_AP_-\n00140)\n[SWS_CORE_10933]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass Errc symbol\n⌈\nAll subclasses\nof\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nshall contain in their scope a type alias called\nErrc\nthat refers to the error condition enumeration defined by [SWS_CORE_10900].\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10934]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass Exception symbol\n⌈\nAll sub-\nclasses of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nshall contain in their scope a type alias called\nException\nthat refers to the exception base type defined by [SWS_CORE_10910].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nAll\nErrorDomain\nsubclasses are usable from within constant expressions, see\n[SWS_CORE_10400]. In particular, this includes that\nErrorDomain\nsubclasses can\nbe defined as\nconstexpr\nglobal variables.\nIn order to further ease working with error domains, all member functions of the\nEr-\nrorDomain\nsubclass are required to be\nnoexcept\n, with the obvious exception of\nara::core::ErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10950]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass member function property\n⌈\nWith the exception of\nara::core::ErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\n, all pub-\nlic member functions of all\nErrorDomain\nsubclasses shall be\nnoexcept\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\nThe virtual member function\nara::core::ErrorDomain::Name\nreturns the short-\nname of the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n, mostly for logging purposes.\n[SWS_CORE_10951]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass shortname retrieval\n⌈\nThe\nreturn value of an error domain's\nara::core::ErrorDomain::Name\nmember func-\ntion shall be equal to the shortname of the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00130)\nEach error domain has an identifier that is used to determine equality of error domains.\nThe error domains that are pre-defined by the Adaptive Platform have standardized\nidentifiers. Application-specific error domains should make sure their identifiers are\nsystem-wide unique.\n[SWS_CORE_10952]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass unique identifier retrieval\n⌈\nThe return value of an error domain's\nara::core::ErrorDomain::Id\nmem-\n34 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nber function shall be a unique identifier that follows the rules defined by\n[SWS_CORE_00010].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nAn\nErrorDomain\ncan transform an\nErrorCode\ninto an exception.\n[SWS_CORE_10953]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nThrowing ErrorCodes as exceptions\n⌈\nThe type of\nan exception thrown by the\nErrorDomain\nsubclass's implementation of\nara::-\ncore::ErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\nshall derive from that\nErrorDomain\nsubclass's\nException\ntype alias defined by [SWS_CORE_10934].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.1.7.4 Global ErrorDomain subclass accessor function\nA global accessor function for the new error domain class is to be defined. For an\nerror domain class\nMyErrorDomain\n, the accessor function is named\nGetMyError-\nDomain\n. This accessor function returns a reference to a single global instance of\nthat class. This accessor function shall be fully\nconstexpr\n-capable; this in turn im-\nplies that the\nErrorDomain\nsubclass also shall be\nconstexpr\n-constructible (see\n[SWS_CORE_10400]).\n[SWS_CORE_10980]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass accessor function\n⌈\nFor all\nsubclasses of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\n, there shall be a global\nconstexpr\nfunc-\ntion that returns a reference-to-const to a singleton instance of it.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10981]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass accessor function naming\n⌈\nAll\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nsubclass accessor functions shall follow the naming\nscheme\nGet<SN>ErrorDomain\n, where\n<SN>\nis the shortname of the\nApApplica-\ntionErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10982]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorDomain subclass accessor function\n⌈\nAll\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nsubclass accessor functions shall have a return type of\nconst ErrorDomain&\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.1.7.5 Global MakeErrorCode overload\nAnd finally, a global factory function\nMakeErrorCode\nneeds to be defined, which is\nimplicitly used by the convenience constructors of class\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\nThis factory function will make use of the global accessor function for the error domain\nsubclass, and call the type-erased constructor of class\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10990]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nMakeErrorCode overload for new error domains\n⌈\nFor all subclasses of\nara::core::ErrorDomain\n, there shall be a\nconstexpr\noverload of the global function\nMakeErrorCode\nthat creates an\nara::core::Er-\nrorCode\ninstance for a given error condition value within the\nara::core::Error-\nDomain\nsubclass's error condition range.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10991]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nMakeErrorCode overload signature\n⌈\nAll overloads\nof the global function\nMakeErrorCode\nshall have the following signature:\n35 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P36_86",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
