      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n1\nconstexpr ErrorCode MakeErrorCode(<SN>Errc code, ErrorDomain::\nSupportDataType data) noexcept;\nwhere\n<SN>\nis the shortname of the\nApApplicationErrorDomain\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\n7.2.1.7.6 C++ pseudo code example\nThe following C++ pseudo code illustrates how these definitions come together:\n1\nnamespace my\n2\n{\n3\n4\nenum class <SN>Errc : ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType\n5\n{\n6\n// ...\n7\n};\n8\n9\nclass <SN>Exception : public ara::core::Exception\n10\n{\n11\npublic:\n12\n<SN>Exception(ara::core::ErrorCode err) noexcept;\n13\n};\n14\n15\nclass <SN>ErrorDomain final : public ara::core::ErrorDomain\n16\n{\n17\npublic:\n18\nusing Errc = <SN>Errc;\n19\nusing Exception = <SN>Exception;\n20\n21\nconstexpr <SN>ErrorDomain() noexcept;\n22\n23\nconst char\n*\nName() const noexcept override;\n24\nconst char\n*\nMessage(ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType errorCode)\nconst noexcept override;\n25\nvoid ThrowAsException(const ara::core::ErrorCode& errorCode) const\nnoexcept(false) override;\n26\n};\n27\n28\nconstexpr const ara::core::ErrorDomain& Get<SN>ErrorDomain() noexcept;\n29\n30\nconstexpr ara::core::ErrorCode MakeErrorCode(<SN>Errc code, ara::core::\nErrorDomain::SupportDataType data) noexcept;\n31\n32\n} // namespace my\n7.2.1.8 AUTOSAR error domains\nThe full range of unique error domain identifiers is partitioned into a range of\nAUTOSAR-specified IDs, another range of vendor-defined IDs, and another range of\nuser-defined IDs.\n36 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P37_87",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00010",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 37,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nUser-defined IDs have their top-bit set to 0 and can use the remaining 63 bits to provide\nuniqueness. IDs with their top-bit set to 1 are reserved for AUTOSAR and stack vendor\nuse.\n[SWS_CORE_00010]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nError domain identifier\n⌈\nAll error domains shall have\na system-wide unique identifier that is represented as a 64-bit unsigned integer value.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_00011]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nAUTOSAR error domain range\n⌈\nError domain identi-\nfiers where bit #63 is set to 1 and bit #62 is set to 0 are reserved for AUTOSAR-defined\nerror domains.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_00016]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nVendor-defined error domain range\n⌈\nError domain\nidentifiers where the top 32 bits (i.e. bit #63..#32) are equal to 0xc000'0000 are re-\nserved for vendor-specific error domains. Bits #31..#16 hold the vendor's numerical\nidentifier, and bits #15..#0 can be used by each vendor for error domain identifiers.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_00013] The Future error domain\n⌈\nThere shall be an error domain\nara::core::FutureErrorDomain\nfor all errors originating from the interaction of\nthe classes\nara::core::Future\nand\nara::core::Promise\n. It shall have the\nshortname\nFuture\nand the identifier 0x8000'0000'0000'0013.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_00014] The Core error domain\n⌈\nThere shall be an error domain\nara::core::CoreErrorDomain\nfor errors originating from non-\nFuture\n/\nPromise\nfacilities of\nara::core\n. It shall have the shortname\nCore\nand the identifier\n0x8000'0000'0000'0014.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.2 Async signal safety\nAn\nasync-signal-safe\nfunction is one that can be safely called from within a POSIX\nsignal handler.\n[6, The POSIX standard] defines a set of functions that are guaranteed to be async-\nsignal-safe; all functions not on that list need to be assumed unsuitable to be called\nwithin a signal handler. This includes all ARA APIs, as it is not specified (and in general\nnot possible to determine) which other functions (whether from POSIX or from other\nstandards or implementations) are called within them.\nUsage of any ARA API within a signal handler will result in undefined behavior of the\napplication, unless otherwise specified.\n7.2.3 Explicit Operation Abortion\nIf a\nViolation\nhas been detected by the implementation of an API function,\n[SWS_CORE_00003] mandates to abort this operation immediately. It allows two ways\n37 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P38_88",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_12402",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nto do this; either by throwing certain kinds of exceptions (if the implementation supports\nC++ exceptions), or by calling\nara::core::Abort\n.\nCalling\nara::core::Abort\nwill result in an\nExplicit Operation Abortion\n,\nwhich usually leads to an\nUnexpected Termination\nas defined by [7]. This section\ndefines the behavior of this mechanism.\nLike\nstd::abort\n, calling\nara::core::Abort\nis meant to terminate the current pro-\ncess abnormally and immediately, without performing stack unwinding and without call-\ning destructors of static objects.\n[SWS_CORE_12402]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nNoreturn property for Abort\n⌈\nThe function\nara:-\n:core::Abort\nshall not return to its caller.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12403]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nLogging of Explicit Operation Abortion\n⌈\nCalling\nara::core::Abort\nshall result in a log message, which shall contain the string that\nhas been passed to the function as argument, being output to the process's standard\nerror stream.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12407]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nThread-safety of Explicit Operation Abortion\n⌈\nWhile a call to\nara::core::Abort\nis in progress, other calls to this function shall\nblock the calling threads.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nara::core::Abort\nprovides a means to add a hook into the system, by calling\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n, similar to the way\nstd::atexit\nallows to install\na callback for the\nstd::exit\nmechanism. Unlike\nstd::atexit\n, however, it is only\npossible to set exactly\none\nhandler with\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n.\n[SWS_CORE_12404]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nAbortHandler invocation\n⌈\nCalling\nara::core::-\nAbort\nshall invoke the\nAbortHandler\n if it has been set  after the log message as\nper [SWS_CORE_12403] has been output.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.3.1 AbortHandler\nThis handler can be installed with\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n. It is invoked in\nturn when\nara::core::Abort\nis called, and it may perform arbitrary operations and\nthen has these four principal choices for its final statements: it can either\n•\nterminate the process, or\n•\nreturn from the function call, or\n•\ndefer function return by entering an infinite loop, or\n•\nperform a non-local goto operation such as\nstd::longjmp\n.\nThe use of non-local goto operations, including\nstd::longjmp\n, is strongly discour-\naged and also expressively prohibited by MISRA, the AUTOSAR C++14 Coding Guide-\nlines, and most other coding guidelines as well.\n38 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P39_89",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_12405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nSimilarly, deferring function return by entering an infinite loop is discouraged as well;\nwhile this still leads to the desired outcome that the\noperation\nwhich caused a\nViola-\ntion\nhas been aborted, it will do so at the cost of defunct'ing the calling thread and\nrisking the destabilization of the software, which already has encountered a\nViola-\ntion\n.\nAn\nAbortHandler\nthat terminates the process is strongly advised to do so by calling\nstd::abort\n. This will make sure that the\nUnexpected Termination\nis properly\nseen by Execution Management as an\nAbnormal Termination\nas well.\nIf the\nAbortHandler\nreturns, or if no\nAbortHandler\nis defined at all, then the final\naction of\nara::core::Abort\nis to call\nstd::abort\n.\n[SWS_CORE_12405]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nFinal action without AbortHandler\n⌈\nIf there is no\ncustom\nara::core::AbortHandler\nthat has been installed with\nara::core:-\n:SetAbortHandler\n, then the implementation of\nara::core::Abort\nshall call\nstd::abort()\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12406]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nFinal action with a returning AbortHandler\n⌈\nIf there\nis a custom\nara::core::AbortHandler\nthat has been installed with\nara::core:-\n:SetAbortHandler\nand it returns, then the implementation of\nara::core::Abort\nshall call\nstd::abort()\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.3.2 SIGABRT handler\nIn addition to the\nara::core::AbortHandler\n, or alternatively to it, the application\ncan also influence this mechanism by installing a signal handler for SIGABRT.\nThe signal handler for SIGABRT has the same choices of actions as the\nara::core:-\n:AbortHandler\n: it can terminate the process, return from the function call, defer\nfunction return by entering an infinite loop, or perform a non-local goto operation. The\nsame caveats as for the\nara::core::AbortHandler\napply here: non-local goto\noperations and infinite loops should be avoided.\nIf the SIGABRT handler does not return, it should in general terminate abnormally\nwith SIGABRT. To do this without entering an infinite loop, it should restore the default\ndisposition of SIGABRT with\nstd::signal(SIGABRT, SIG_DFL)\nand then re-raise\nSIGABRT with e.g.\nstd::raise(SIGABORT)\n.\nThis second step of influence that the SIGABRT handler provides allows applications\nthat are already handling other synchronous signals such as SIGSEGV or SIGFPE to\ntreat SIGABRT the same way.\n39 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P40_90",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10200",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 40,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2.4 Advanced data types\n7.2.4.1 AUTOSAR types\n7.2.4.1.1 InstanceSpecifier\nInstances of\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nare used to identify service port\nprototype instances within the AUTOSAR meta-model and are therefore used in the\nara::com\nAPI and elsewhere. A detailed description and background can be found\nin [8] sections 6.1 (Instance Identifiers) and 9.4.4 (Usage of meta-model identifiers\nwithin ara::com based application code).\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\ncan conceptually be understood to be a wrapper\nfor a string representation of a valid meta-model path. It is designed to be either con-\nstructed from a string representation via a factory method\nara::core::Instance-\nSpecifier::Create\n, which provides an exception-free solution, or directly by using\nthe constructor, which might throw an exception if the string representation is invalid.\n[SWS_CORE_10200] Valid InstanceSpecifier representations\n⌈\nThe content of a\nvalid\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nconsists of a \"/\"-separated list of model el-\nement names starting from an\nExecutable\nto the respective\nPortPrototype\nto\nwhich the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nshall apply.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10201] Validation of meta-model paths\n⌈\nThe construction mech-\nanisms of class\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nshall reject meta-model\npaths that are syntactically invalid according to the syntax rules defined in\n[SWS_CORE_10200].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10202] Construction of InstanceSpecifier objects\n⌈\nAPIs for con-\nstruction of\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nobjects shall be available in both\npotentially-throwing and non-throwing form.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.4.1.2 ScaleLinearAndTexttable\nA\nara::core::ScaleLinearAndTexttable\ntype is a struct type that emulates an\nenumeration type with extended capabilities, such as those given in [9, the C++17\nstandard]\nIn particular, it can hold the values of the enumeration, but also any value of the under-\nlying type of the Enumeration Data Type with which it was defined.\n7.2.4.2 Types derived from the base C++ standard\nIn addition to AUTOSAR-devised data types, which are mentioned in the previous sec-\ntions, the Adaptive Platform also contains a number of generic data types and helper\nfunctions.\n40 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P41_91",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00040",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 41,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nSome types are already contained in [4, the C++14 standard]; however, types with al-\nmost identical behavior are re-defined within the\nara::core\nnamespace. The reason\nfor this is that the memory allocation behavior of the\nstd::\ntypes is often unsuitable\nfor automotive purposes. Thus, the\nara::core\nones define their own memory allo-\ncation behavior, and perform some other necessary adaptions as well, including about\nthe throwing of exceptions.\n[SWS_CORE_00040]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrors originating from C++ standard classes\n⌈\nFor\nthe classes in ara::core specified below in terms of the corresponding classes of the\nC++ standard, all functions that are specified by [4, the C++14 standard], [9, the C++17\nstandard], or [10, the draft C++20 standard] to throw any exceptions, are instead spec-\nified to be the cause of a\nViolation\nwhen they do so.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nExamples for such data types are: Array, Vector, Map, and String.\n7.2.4.2.1 Array\nThis section describes the\nara::core::Array\ntype that represents a container\nwhich encapsulates fixed size arrays.\nara::core::Array\nis an almost-equivalent of\nstd::array\n, and most type proper-\nties of\nstd::array\napply to\nara::core::Array\nas well.\nThese differences to\nstd::array\nare intended:\n•\nstd::array::at\nhas been omitted (in order to avoid mandatory exception han-\ndling)\n[SWS_CORE_11200] Array base behavior\n⌈\nara::core::Array\nand all its member\nfunctions and supporting constructs shall behave identical to those of header\n<array>\nfrom [4, the C++14 standard], except for the differences specified in this document.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.4.2.2 SteadyClock\n7.2.4.2.2.1 Definitions of terms\nThe C++\nstd::chrono\nlibrary defines a number of concepts and types for handling\ntime and durations. One of these concepts is that of a clock which is able to create\nsnapshots of specific time points. When talking about clocks and time points, the\nthree qualities\nresolution\n,\nprecision\n, and\naccuracy\nare distinguished within this docu-\nment as follows:\n•\nThe\nresolution\nrelates to the smallest increment that can be expressed with\nthe clock's measurement data type.\n41 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P42_92",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nFor clocks of the POSIX\nclock_gettime\nAPI, the\nresolution\nis implicitly de-\nfined as nanoseconds by the API's usage of\nstruct timespec\nwith its\ntime-\nspec::tv_nsec\nfield.\nFor C++ clocks of the\nstd::chrono\nAPIs, the\nresolution\nis variable.\n•\nThe\nprecision\nof a clock is the smallest time interval that its timer is able to\nmeasure. The\nprecision\nis implementation-defined and depends on the prop-\nerties and capabilities of the physical machine as well as the operating system.\n•\nThe\naccuracy\nof a clock is the relation between the reported value and the truth.\nIn addition to that, the\nepoch\nis an important property of a clock as well, as it defines\nthe base of the time range that can originate from a clock. Clocks that measure cal-\nendar time often use Unix time, which is given as number of seconds (without leap\nseconds) since the Unix Epoch, which is 1970-01-01, 00:00:00 UTC.\nClocks that place more emphasis on high\nprecision\noften do not relate to calendar\ntime at all, but generate timestamps as offsets from something like the power-up time\nof the system.\n7.2.4.2.2.2 Clocks in the Adaptive Platform\nThe C++\nstd::chrono\nlibrary defines a number of standard clocks. Amongst these\nis\nstd::chrono::steady_clock\n, which represents a monotonic clock whose time\npoints are strictly increasing with a fixed interval.\nHowever, the C++ standard does not place any requirements on the\nresolution\n,\nprecision\n, and\naccuracy\nof this clock. The undefinedness of its\nresolution\ncan\npose some difficulties for application programmers, but these can usually be solved\nby agreeing on a common  or minimum \nresolution\n. The\nprecision\nand\nac-\ncuracy\nare always dependent on the physical properties of the machine and of the\noperating system.\nThe Adaptive Platform defines\nara::core::SteadyClock\nas a\nstd::chrono\n-\ncompatible clock with nanosecond\nresolution\nand a\nstd::int64_t\ndatatype. Its\nprecision\nand\naccuracy\nare still implementation-defined and can be given as char-\nacteristic values of a concrete platform. Its\nepoch\nis the power-up time of the ECU.\nWith these properties, timestamps generated by\nara::core::SteadyClock\nwill not\noverflow until 292 years after its\nepoch\n.\nIt is the standard clock of the Adaptive Platform and should be used for most timekeep-\ning purposes.\nThe properties of\nara::core::SteadyClock\nimply that a type alias to\nstd::chrono::steady_clock\nis a conforming implementation of\nara::core:-\n:SteadyClock\n, if\nstd::chrono::steady_clock::period\nis equivalent to\nstd::nano\n, and\nstd::chrono::steady_clock::rep\nis a 64-bit signed integer\ntype such as\nstd::int64_t\n.\n42 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P43_93",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_11800",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 43,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_11800] SteadyClock type requirements\n⌈\nClass\nara::core::-\nSteadyClock\nshall meet the requirements of\nTrivialClock\nfrom [4, the C++14 stan-\ndard].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_11801] Epoch of SteadyClock\n⌈\nThe\nepoch\nof\nara::core::-\nSteadyClock\nshall be the system start-up.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.4.3 Types derived from newer C++ standards\nThese types have been defined in or proposed for a newer C++ standard, and the\nAdaptive Platform includes them into the\nara::core\nnamespace, usually because\nthey are necessary for certain constructs of the Manifest.\nExamples for such data types are: Optional, StringView, Span, and Variant.\n7.2.4.3.1 ara::core::Byte\nara::core::Byte\nis a type that is able to hold a byte of the machine. It is an own\ntype distinct from any other type.\nThe definitions of this section have been carefully set up in a way to make\nstd::byte\nfrom [9, the C++17 standard] a conforming implementation, but also allow a class-\nbased implementation with only C++14 means.\nUnlike\nstd::byte\nfrom [9, the C++17 standard], it is implementation-defined whether\nara::core::Byte\ncan be used for type aliasing without triggering Undefined Behav-\nior.\n[SWS_CORE_10100] Type property of ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe type\nara:-\n:core::Byte\nshall not be an integral type. In particular, the value\nstd::is_integral<ara::core::Byte>::value\nshall be 0.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10101] Size of type ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe size (in bytes) of an instance\nof type\nara::core::Byte\n(determined with\nsizeof(ara::core::Byte)\n) shall be\n1.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10102] Value range of type ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe value of\nan instance of type\nara::core::Byte\nshall be constrained to the range\n[0..std::numeric_limits<unsigned char>::max()]\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10103] Creation of ara::core::Byte instances\n⌈\nAn instance of type\nara::core::Byte\nshall be creatable from an integral type with brace-initialization\nsyntax. This initialization shall also be possible when called in a constant expres-\nsion. If the initializer value is outside the value range of type\nara::core::Byte\n(see\n[SWS_CORE_10102]), the behavior is undefined.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10104] Default-constructed ara::core::Byte instances\n⌈\nAn instance\nof type\nara::core::Byte\nshall be constructible without giving an initializer value.\n43 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P44_94",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10105",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 44,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nSuch a variable definition shall incur no runtime cost, and the value of the instance\nshall have indeterminate content.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10105] Destructor of type ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe destructor of type\nara::core::Byte\nshall be trivial.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10106] Implicit conversion from other types\n⌈\nThe type\nara::-\ncore::Byte\nshall not be implicitly convertible from any other type.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10107] Implicit conversion to other types\n⌈\nThe type\nara::core:-\n:Byte\nshall allow no implicit conversion to any other type, including\nbool\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10108] Conversion to unsigned char\n⌈\nThe type\nara::core::Byte\nshall allow conversion to\nunsigned char\nwith a\nstatic_cast<>\nexpression. This\nconversion shall also be possible when called in a constant expression.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10109] Equality comparison for ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe type\nara::-\ncore::Byte\nshall be comparable for equality with other instances of type\nara::-\ncore::Byte\n. This comparison shall also be possible when called in a constant ex-\npression.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10110] Non-equality comparison for ara::core::Byte\n⌈\nThe type\nara::core::Byte\nshall be comparable for non-equality with other instances of type\nara::core::Byte\n. This comparison shall also be possible when called in a constant\nexpression.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.5 Initialization and Shutdown\nThis section describes the global initialization and shutdown of the ARA framework.\nBefore the framework is initialized, and after the it is deinitialized, not all ARA function-\nality may be available.\nWhile it is usually possible for a framework implementation to initialize all parts of the\nframework in an initialize on first use fashion, this might not always be desirable, as it\nintroduces potentially noticeable delays during runtime.\nFor this reason, there exist initialization and shutdown functions that may be used by\nthe framework vendor to initialize/shutdown the framework to an extent that no lazy\ninitialization during runtime is necessary.\nOn the other hand, another framework implementation might well have empty imple-\nmentations of these functions, e.g. if this framework chooses to fully adopt the initialize\non first use idiom.\n[SWS_CORE_15003]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nStartup and initialization of ARA\n⌈\nThe\nara::-\ncore::Initialize\nfunction shall initiate the start-up of the ARA framework, which\nmight include (but is not limited to):\n44 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_95",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_15004",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n•\ninitialization of ARA framework specific data structures\n•\ninitialization of system resources\n•\nspawning of background threads\n⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\n[SWS_CORE_15004]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nShutdown and de-initialization of ARA\n⌈\nThe\nara:-\n:core::Deinitialize\nfunction shall initiate the shutdown of the ARA framework,\nwhich might include (but is not limited to):\n•\norderly shutdown of spawned background threads\n•\ndeallocation of dynamically allocated memory\n•\ndeallocation of other system resources\n⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\nAn error returned by\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis the only way for the ARA to re-\nport an error that is guaranteed to be available, e.g. in case\nara::log\nhas already\nbeen deinitialized. The user is not expected to be able to recover from such an error.\nHowever, the user may have a project-specific way of recording errors during deinitial-\nization without\nara::log\n. A typical error case to be reported here is that the user is\nstill holding some resource from the ARA.\nCalling\nara::core::Deinitialize\nwhile ARA APIs are still being called concur-\nrently results in undefined behavior of the application and the framework.\nFor a proper shutdown, it is also expected that\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis called\nbefore the statically initialized data is destructed.\n[SWS_CORE_15001]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nHandling of interaction with the ARA of an un-\n/deinitialized runtime\n⌈\nA call to any ARA API (other than the ones mentioned\nin [SWS_CORE_15002]) without prior call to\nara::core::Initialize\nshall be\ntreated by the Functional Cluster implementation as a\nViolation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nThe rationale to treat this as a\nViolation\nis that such occurrences cannot be handled\nby the caller of the API at the point in time where the error is detected. Aborting exe-\ncution is the only way to signal this kind of systematic error and prevent later failures.\n[SWS_CORE_15002]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSpecial ara::core types to be used without initial-\nization\n⌈\nA small subset of\nara::core\ntypes and functions shall be usable indepen-\ndently of initialization with\nara::core::Initialize\n. These are:\n•\nara::core::ErrorCode\nand all its member functions and supporting con-\nstructs (including global operators)\n•\nara::core::StringView\nand all its member functions and supporting con-\nstructs (including global operators)\n•\nara::core::Result\nand all its member functions and supporting constructs,\nexcept for\nara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow\n45 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_96",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10400",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n•\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nand all its member functions and its subclasses,\nas long as they adhere to [SWS_CORE_10400], but excluding\n<Prefix>Er-\nrorDomain::ThrowAsException\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nThe rationale for the exception for this subset is the intended use before initialization\nand that these types are used as part of the initialization (\nara::core::Result\n,\nara::core::ErrorCode\n,\nara::core::ErrorDomain\n).\n46 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },

      "source_page": 88,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n8.1.6\nFuture\nand\nPromise\ndata types\nThis section describes the\nFuture\nand\nPromise\nclass templates used in\nara::core\nto provide and retrieve the results of asynchronous method calls.\nWhenever there is a mention of a standard C++14 item (class, class template, enum\nor function) such as\nstd::future\nor\nstd::promise\n, the implied source material\nis [4]. Whenever there is a mention of an experimental C++ item such as\nstd::-\nexperimental::future::is_ready\n, the implied source material is [11].\n88 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P89_340",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00400",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 89,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nFutures are technically referred to as asynchronous return objects, and Promises\nare referred to as asynchronous providers. Their interaction is made possible by a\nshared state. The shared state concept is described in [4], section 30.6.4. The\ndescription also applies to the shared state behind\nara::core::Future\nand\nara:-\n:core::Promise\n, with the following changes:\n•\nThe text\n, as used by async when policy is\nlaunch::deferred\n\nis removed\nfrom paragraph 2.\n•\nParagraph 10, referring to\n\npromise::set_value_at_thread_exit\n\n, is re-\nmoved.\nClass\nara::core::Future\nand\nara::core::Promise\nare closely modeled on\nstd::future\nand\nstd::promise\n. Consequently, the behavior of\nara::core:-\n:Future\nand\nara::core::Promise\nis expected to be same as that of\nstd::-\nfuture\nand\nstd::promise\nfrom [4, the C++14 standard] and the corresponding\nstd::experimental::\nclasses from [11], except for the deviations from the\nstd::\nclasses that result from the integration with\nara::core::Result\n.\n8.1.6.1\nfuture_errc\nenumeration\n[SWS_CORE_00400]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_543",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,

    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_544",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Overload of std::swap for ara::core::Array."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_545",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n8.1.7.3 Tuple interface\nThese definitions implement the standard interface of tuple-like types for class\nArray\n.\nThe specializations of the\nstd::tuple_size\nand\nstd::tuple_element\ntraits are\nput into the\nstd\nnamespace:\n[SWS_CORE_01280]\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_546",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "tuple_size< ara::core::Array< T, N > >"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_547",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "template <typename T, size_t N>\nstruct tuple_size< ara::core::Array< T, N > > : public integral_\nconstant< size_t, N > {...};"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_548",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specialization of std::tuple_size for ara::core::Array.\nThis specialization shall meet the C++14 UnaryTypeTrait requirements with a Base\nCharacteristic of std::integral_constant<std::size_t, N>."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_549",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_01281]\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P126_550",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_01280",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 126,

Its interface shall be equivalent to:\ntemplate <typename Allocator>\nvoid swap(BasicString<Allocator>& lhs, BasicString<Allocator>& rhs);\nThis function shall exchange the state of lhs with that of rhs.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n8.1.14\nSpan\ndata type\nThis section describes the\nara::core::Span\ntype that constitutes a view over a\ncontiguous sequence of objects, the storage of which is owned by another object.\nThis specification is based on the draft standard of\nstd::span\nin revision N4835 (sec-\ntion 22.7), but has been adapted in several ways:\n•\nThe type alias\nSpan::index_type\nhas been renamed into\nSpan::-\nsize_type\n, following the P1872R0 proposal.\n•\nSome compile-time checks are now being imposed on implementations, following\nthe proposed resolution of LWG issue 3103.\n•\nAll symbols from section 22.7.3.8 (span.tuple) have been omitted, following the\nproposed resolution of LWG issue 3212.\n•\nThe\nstd::array\n-based constructors have been made more flexible, following\nthe proposed resolution of LWG issue 3255.\n•\nConstructors have been added that take a\nara::core::Array\n, with semantics\nthat are the same as those of the constructors that take a\nstd::array\n.\n•\nA number of global\nMakeSpan\nfactory function overloads have been added.\n[SWS_CORE_01901]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\n137 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Construct a new Span from the given container.\n[ara::core::data(cont), ara::core::data(cont) + ara::core::size(cont)) shall be a valid range.\nThis constructor shall not participate in overload resolution unless: extent == dynamic_extent is\ntrue, Container is not a specialization of Span, Container is not a specialization of Array,\nContainer is not a specialization of std::array, std::is_array<Container>::value is false,\nara::core::data(cont) and ara::core::size(cont) are both well-formed, and std::remove_pointer_\nt<decltype(ara::core::data(cont))>(*)[] is convertible to T(*)[]."

      "source_page": 145,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Construct a new Span from the given const container.\n[ara::core::data(cont), ara::core::data(cont) + ara::core::size(cont)) shall be a valid range.\nThis constructor shall not participate in overload resolution unless: extent == dynamic_extent is\ntrue, Container is not a specialization of Span, Container is not a specialization of Array,\nContainer is not a specialization of std::array, std::is_array<Container>::value is false,\nara::core::data(cont) and ara::core::size(cont) are both well-formed, and std::remove_\npointer<decltype(ara::core::data(cont))>::type(*)[] is convertible to T(*)[]."
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nThese global functions allow to convert a\nSpan<T>\ninto a\nSpan<Byte>\n, thereby\ngaining access to the in-memory representation of the object referenced by a\nSpan\ninstance.\nUnlike\nstd::byte\nfrom [9, the C++17 standard], it is implementation-defined whether\nara::core::Byte\ncan be used for type aliasing without triggering Undefined Be-\nhavior. This may also affect\nara::core::as_bytes\nand\nara::core::as_-\nwritable_bytes\nin particular. Implementations usually provide a way to make this\nsafe by loosening the aliasing restrictions of the C++ compiler.\n[SWS_CORE_01980]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 175,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n8.1.18 Generic helpers\n8.1.18.1 ara::core::Byte\nThe exact setup of this type is implementation-defined; the specifications in section\n7.2.4.3.1 (ara::core::Byte) define the expected behavior.\n[SWS_CORE_04200]\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P175_781",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_04200",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 175,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n8.1.18.2 In-place disambiguation tags\nThe data types\nara::core::in_place_t\n,\nara::core::in_place_type_t\n, and\nara::core::in_place_index_t\nare disambiguation tags that can be passed to\ncertain constructors of\nara::core::Optional\nand\nara::core::Variant\nto in-\ndicate that the contained type shall be constructed in-place, i.e. without any copy\noperation taking place.\nThey are equivalent to\nstd::in_place_t\n,\nstd::in_place_type_t\n, and\nstd::-\nin_place_index_t\nfrom [9]. All these symbols are provided here in order to give\nthe necessary support for implementing\nara::core::Optional\nand\nara::core:-\n:Variant\nin a way that is highly compatible with the corresponding classes from [9,\nthe C++17 standard].\n175 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P176_782",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_04011",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 176,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n8.1.18.2.1\nin_place_t\ntag\n[SWS_CORE_04011]\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P176_783",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_04011",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 176,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Denote an operation to be performed in-place.\nAn instance of this type can be passed to certain constructors of ara::core::Optional to denote\nthe intention that construction of the contained type shall be done in-place, i.e. without any\ncopying taking place."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P176_784",

      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n8.1.19 Initialization and Shutdown\nThis section describes the global initialization and shutdown functions that initialize\nresp. deinitialize data structures and threads of the AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nApplications.\n[SWS_CORE_10001]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_812",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "(Pre-)Initialization of the ARA Framework.\nPrior to this call, interaction with the ARA is not allowed with the exception of types intended to\nbe used independently of initialization: ara::core::ErrorCode, ara::core::StringView,\nara::core::Result but not the function ValueOrThrow, ara::core::ErrorDomain and subclasses,\nbut not the function ThrowAsException. It is strongly recommended to make this call in a place\nwhere it is guaranteed that static initialization has completed."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_813",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\n[SWS_CORE_10002]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_814",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Shutdown of the ARA Framework.\nAfter this call, no interaction with the ARA is allowed with the exception of types intendent to be\nused independently of initialization: ara::core::ErrorCode, ara::core::StringView,\nara::core::Result but not the function ValueOrThrow, ara::core::ErrorDomain and subclasses,\nbut not the function ThrowAsException. As a prerequisite to calling this API it is expected that\nthe use of ARA interfaces is completed (with the given exceptions). It is strongly recommended\nto make this call in a place where it is guaranteed that the static initialization has completed and\ndestruction of statically initialized data has not yet started."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_815",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\n8.1.20 Abnormal process termination\nThis section describes the APIs that constitute the explicit abnormal termination facility.\n[SWS_CORE_00053]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\n182 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P183_816",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00050",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 183,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P183_817",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00050",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 183,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "A function declaration with the correct prototype for SetAbortHandler().\nThis declaration exists only for providing a function type that includes \"noexcept\" and that acts\nas base type for a type alias, which is defined in SWS_CORE_00050.\nThis compensates for the fact that the C++ standard (up to and including C++14) prohibits that\n\"noexcept\" appears in an alias-declaration.\nThere is no implementation of this function."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nA Mentioned Manifest Elements\nFor the sake of completeness, this chapter contains a set of class tables representing\nmeta-classes mentioned in the context of this document but which are not contained\ndirectly in the scope of describing specific meta-model semantics.\nChapter is generated."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P187_827",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 187,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nB.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces\nwhich are accessible by user space applications (see chapter 8 (API specification))\ncan also be used for interaction between Functional Clusters.\nThe goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-\nteraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between\ndocuments specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-\ntion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform\nprovider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.\nB.2 Interface Tables\nB.2.1 Functional Cluster initialization\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Deinitialize\ninitialize and deini-\ntialize other Functional Clusters as necessary for the particular implementation. All\nFunctional Clusters where this is necessary thus need to provide internal interfaces for\ntheir initialization and deinitialization.\nC History of Specification Items\nPlease note that the lists in this chapter also include specification items that have been\nremoved from the specification in a later version. These specification items do not\nappear as hyperlinks in the document.\n187 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h3>Rolle &amp; Verwendungszweck</h3><p>Das Modul <code>ara::core</code> stellt das fundamentale Basis- und Laufzeitfundament der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform dar. Es definiert den gemeinsamen Standard für Datentypen, Fehlerbehandlungsmuster, asynchrone Kontrollflüsse und Lebenszyklusfunktionen über alle Functional Clusters sowie für anwendungsspezifischen Adaptive-Code hinweg <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00001\">[SWS_CORE_00001]</a>. Um in sicherheitskritischen automobilen Steuergeräten deterministisches Verhalten zu garantieren, ersetzt <code>ara::core</code> traditionelle C++-Mechanismen wie unkontrollierte Exception-Weitergabe oder nicht echtzeitfähige Standard-Allokatoren durch explizite Typverträge.</p><p>Die Kernaufgaben von <code>ara::core</code> umfassen:</p><ul><li><strong>Einheitliches Fehlermodell:</strong> Bereitstellung von <code>ara::core::Result&lt;T, E&gt;</code> und <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> zur expliziten, typsicheren und ausnahmelosen Rückgabe von Fehlern im regulären Kontrollfluss.</li><li><strong>Asynchronitätsmuster:</strong> Standardisierung von <code>ara::core::Future</code> und <code>ara::core::Promise</code> als konsistente Brücke für nebenläufige und verteilte Berechnungen in allen AUTOSAR-AP-Schnittstellen.</li><li><strong>Port- und Instanzabstraktion:</strong> Bereitstellung des Typs <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code>, der logische Software-Architektur-Modellelemente auf konkrete Plattform- und Kommunikationskonfigurationen abbildet.</li><li><strong>Lebenszyklus-Initialisierung:</strong> Zentraler Einstiegspunkt über <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> für das Hoch- und Herunterfahren der Adaptive Platform im Anwendungsprozess.</li><li><strong>Automotive-fähige Hilfs- und Container-Typen:</strong> Typen wie <code>Span</code>, <code>StringView</code>, <code>Optional</code> und <code>Variant</code> zur ressourcenschonenden, kopierfreien Datenübergabe.</li></ul><h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3><p>Alle öffentlichen ARA-Schnittstellen (AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive Applications) basieren zwingend auf den Typverträgen von <code>ara::core</code>. Die Spezifikation unterscheidet dabei funktionale Datenstrukturen, Identifikatoren und Fehlerbehandlungsprimitive:</p><ul><li><strong>Initialisierungsvertrag:</strong> Vor dem Aufruf jeglicher funktionaler ARA-APIs muss der Prozess <code>ara::core::Initialize()</code> aufrufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00701\">[SWS_CORE_00701]</a>. Dieser Aufruf initialisiert interne Laufzeitstrukturen, Log-Sinks und abhängige Cluster. Vor Beendigung des Prozesses ist korrespondierend <code>ara::core::Deinitialize()</code> aufzurufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00801\">[SWS_CORE_00801]</a>.</li><li><strong>Result- und Fehlervertrag:</strong> Operationen, die fehlschlagen können, liefern ein <code>ara::core::Result&lt;T, E&gt;</code> zurück <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00733\">[SWS_CORE_00733]</a>. Ein <code>Result</code> kapselt entweder den gewünschten Wert vom Typ <code>T</code> oder einen <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00763\">[SWS_CORE_00763]</a>. Jeder <code>ErrorCode</code> referenziert eine konkrete <code>ErrorDomain</code> mit eindeutiger 64-Bit-Kennung <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00767\">[SWS_CORE_00767]</a>, wodurch Fehlernummern clusterübergreifend kollisionsfrei interpretiert werden.</li><li><strong>Asynchroner Vertrag:</strong> Asynchrone Schnittstellen liefern ein <code>ara::core::Future&lt;T, E&gt;</code> zurück <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00736\">[SWS_CORE_00736]</a>. Aufrufer können synchron auf das Eintreffen warten (<code>wait()</code>, <code>wait_for()</code>) oder über <code>GetResult()</code> das finale <code>Result&lt;T, E&gt;</code> abholen, ohne dass C++-Standardausnahmen geworfen werden.</li><li><strong>Instanzbindung:</strong> Der <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> kapselt einen qualifizierten Manifest-Pfad (z. B. <code>/Executable/PortPrototype</code>) als eindeutigen Schlüssel zur Konfigurationsauflösung <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_08001\">[SWS_CORE_08001]</a>.</li><li><strong>Forwarding-Header:</strong> Der Namensraum <code>ara</code> ist für AUTOSAR reserviert. Um Compile-Zeiten zu optimieren und modulare Abhängigkeiten zu trennen, stellt jeder Cluster Forwarding-Header <code>&lt;fc&gt;_fwd.h</code> bereit.</li></ul><h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3><p>Der Lebenszyklus einer Adaptive Application beginnt typischerweise mit dem Aufruf von <code>Initialize()</code>. Anschließend werden funktionale Cluster wie <code>ara::com</code>, <code>ara::exec</code> oder <code>ara::diag</code> verwendet, wobei asynchrone Schnittstellen durch das Zusammenspiel von <code>Promise</code> und <code>Future</code> synchronisiert werden. Vor dem Prozessende stellt <code>Deinitialize()</code> den geordneten Rückbau aller Cluster-Ressourcen sicher.</p><div class=\"diagram\" id=\"diag-01\"><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" <code>Promise</code> und <code>Future</code>, Fehlerrückgabe via <code>Result</code>/<code>ErrorCode</code> und geordneter Shutdown über <code>Deinitialize()</code>. Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00701\">[SWS_CORE_00701]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00801\">[SWS_CORE_00801]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00733\">[SWS_CORE_00733]</a> und <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00736\">[SWS_CORE_00736]</a>.</p><h3>Konfiguration &amp; Fehlerbehandlung</h3><p>Für Fehler und Ausnahmezustände etabliert <code>ara::core</code> eine strikte Zwei-Klassen-Architektur:</p><ul><li><strong>Behebbare Fehler (Recoverable Errors):</strong> Diese spiegeln erwartbare Fehlerszenarien wider (z. B. Timeout, temporäre Nichtverfügbarkeit eines Dienstes oder ungültige Nutzereingaben). Sie werden über <code>Result&lt;T, E&gt;</code> an den Aufrufer übergeben und müssen von der Fachlogik ausgewertet und behandelt werden <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021\">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a>.</li><li><strong>Unbehebbare Regelverletzungen (Violations):</strong> Violations resultieren aus verletzten Vor- oder Nachbedingungen, Programmierfehlern oder korrumpierten Speicherzuständen des Frameworks. Bei einer Violation bricht das System die Ausführung sofort und unumkehrbar über <code>ara::core::Abort()</code> ab <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00090\">[SWS_CORE_00090]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12404\">[SWS_CORE_12404]</a>. Parallel ankommende Threads blockieren während <code>Abort()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12407\">[SWS_CORE_12407]</a>, um unkontrollierte Kaskadeneffekte zu unterbinden.</li></ul><p>Zur einheitlichen Diagnose und Rückverfolgbarkeit definiert <code>ara::core</code> standardisierte Logging-Kontext-IDs je Funktionscluster, u. a. <code>#COR</code> für Core, <code>#COM</code> für Communication Management, <code>#EXE</code> für Execution Management und <code>#DIA</code> für Diagnostics <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00055\">[SWS_CORE_00055]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90024\">[SWS_CORE_90024]</a>.</p></div>\n",

<div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Einordnung &amp; Zweck</h4>
<p>Das Modul <code>ara::core</code> ist die grundlegende Basisbibliothek der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform und wird in der offiziellen Spezifikation <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#page=60">AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf (R25-11)</a> definiert. Es stellt den fehlerlosen Rückgabetyp <code>ara::core::Result</code> sowie die Fehlerdomänen-Basisklasse <code>ara::core::ErrorDomain</code> bereit, welche den Kontext für eine Menge von Fehlerbedingungen definiert; ErrorDomain-Subklassen sind die Wurzel aller Fehlerdaten <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_10303">[SWS_CORE_10303]</a>. Fehlerbehandlung erfolgt in der Adaptive Platform grundsätzlich ohne C++-Exceptions über <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> und <code>ara::core::Result</code> nach dem „ValueOrError“-Konzept (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Der Namespace <code>ara</code> und alle darunterliegenden Namespaces sind zudem von AUTOSAR reserviert; fügt eine Adaptive Application dort eigene Deklarationen hinzu, ist das Verhalten undefiniert (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Damit bildet <code>ara::core</code> das gemeinsame Fundament für Initialisierung, Fehlerbehandlung und Nebenläufigkeitsregeln aller AP-Funktionscluster.</p>
<h4>Zentrale Objekte und typische Verwendung</h4>
<p><code>ara::core::Result&lt;T, E&gt;</code> enthält entweder einen Wert oder einen Fehler; der Fehlertyp muss <code>ErrorCode</code> sein, sonst liegt ein Compile-Fehler vor <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html">[SWS_CORE_00701]</a>, mit Spezialisierungen für Referenztypen <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_T_E_8b59ba.html">[SWS_CORE_00901]</a> und für <code>void</code>-Werte <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_void_E_c9d1e9.html">[SWS_CORE_00801]</a>. Erzeugt wird ein <code>Result</code> über die statischen Fabrikfunktionen <code>FromValue</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00733">[SWS_CORE_00733]</a> oder <code>FromError</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00736">[SWS_CORE_00736]</a>. <code>Bind</code> wendet ein Callable auf einen enthaltenen Wert an und liefert ein neues <code>Result</code>; enthält die Instanz keinen Wert, wird der ursprüngliche Fehler unverändert übernommen <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00768">[SWS_CORE_00768]</a>. <code>Resolve</code> liefert den Wert oder ruft im Fehlerfall ein kompatibles Callable auf <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00767">[SWS_CORE_00767]</a>, während <code>ErrorOr</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00764">[SWS_CORE_00764]</a><a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00763">[SWS_CORE_00763]</a> einfache Fallback-Werte liefert. <code>ErrorDomain</code>-Instanzen sind genau dann gleich, wenn ihre eindeutigen 64-Bit-Identifier übereinstimmen; der Zugriff erfolgt üblicherweise über Nicht-Member-Accessoren wie <code>GetFutureErrorDomain</code> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_10401">[SWS_CORE_10401]</a>.</p>
<p>Für Container und Textverarbeitung stellt das Modul PMR-fähige Implementierungen der C++-Standardbibliothek bereit: <code>ara::core::Vector</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Vector_53b788.html">[SWS_CORE_01301]</a>, <code>ara::core::Map</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Map_cba7f0.html">[SWS_CORE_01400]</a>, <code>ara::core::StringView</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html">[SWS_CORE_02001]</a>, <code>ara::core::BasicString</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_BasicString_b75ad8.html">[SWS_CORE_03000]</a> und <code>ara::core::Span</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Span_f16d72.html">[SWS_CORE_01900]</a>. Für Modellreferenzen auf Anwendungsebene existiert die <code>final</code>-Klasse <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> in <code>ara/core/instance_specifier.h</code>, die einen AUTOSAR-shortName-Pfad kapselt <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_InstanceSpecifier_4f5967.html">[SWS_CORE_08001]</a>.</p>
<h4>Erzeugung, Lebenszyklus &amp; Ownership</h4>
<p>Der Lebenszyklus der gesamten ARA wird zentral über die beiden freien Funktionen <code>ara::core::Initialize</code> und <code>ara::core::Deinitialize</code> gesteuert. <code>Initialize</code> startet das ARA-Framework; dies kann die Initialisierung interner Datenstrukturen und Systemressourcen sowie das Starten von Hintergrund-Threads umfassen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15003">[SWS_CORE_15003]</a>. Nutzt <code>Initialize</code> die Injektion von Kommandozeilenargumenten, müssen die betreffenden Argumente transparent entfernt werden, damit das Argument-Parsing der Applikation nicht beeinflusst wird <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15006">[SWS_CORE_15006]</a>. Ein erfolgreicher Aufruf versetzt das Framework in einen Zustand, in dem alle konfigurierten Komponenten sofort API-Aufrufe bedienen können <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90026">[SWS_CORE_90026]</a>; ein zweiter Aufruf ohne vorheriges <code>Deinitialize</code> liefert <code>kAlreadyInitialized</code>, ohne die laufende Instanz zu stören <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90029">[SWS_CORE_90029]</a>. <code>Deinitialize</code> startet umgekehrt das Herunterfahren des Frameworks, einschließlich Beendigung gestarteter Hintergrund-Threads und Freigabe dynamischen Speichers sowie weiterer Systemressourcen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15004">[SWS_CORE_15004]</a>; ist das Framework nicht erfolgreich initialisiert oder bereits deinitialisiert, liefert jeder Aufruf <code>kNotInitialized</code> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90030">[SWS_CORE_90030]</a>.</p>
<p>Nur eine kleine, explizit benannte Teilmenge von <code>ara::core</code> – u. a. <code>ErrorCode</code>, <code>StringView</code>, <code>Result</code> (ohne <code>ValueOrThrow</code>), <code>ErrorDomain</code> (ohne <code>ThrowAsException</code>), <code>Initialize</code>, <code>Abort</code>, <code>SetAbortHandler</code> und <code>AddAbortHandler</code> – darf unabhängig von <code>Initialize</code>/<code>Deinitialize</code> benutzt werden <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15002">[SWS_CORE_15002]</a>. Das Verhalten aller anderen ARA-Funktionen vor <code>Initialize</code> ist implementierungsdefiniert <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15005">[SWS_CORE_15005]</a>, und auch ein Aufruf nach <code>Deinitialize</code> außerhalb dieser Teilmenge hat implementierungsdefiniertes Verhalten, da ein entsprechender Laufzeitcheck aus Performancegründen bewusst nicht gefordert wurde <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90022">[SWS_CORE_90022]</a>. Die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">Guidelines for using Adaptive Platform interfaces</a> fassen dies als verbindlichen Startup/Shutdown-Vertrag: <code>Initialize</code> ist am Einsprungpunkt aufzurufen, <code>Deinitialize</code> erst nachdem alle ARA-Ressourcen auch in anderen Threads freigegeben wurden; beide liefern <code>Result&lt;void&gt;</code>, das geprüft werden muss, und ein Fehler ist nicht behebbar, sodass die Applikation mit <code>EXIT_FAILURE</code> terminieren muss (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Ergänzend untersagt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a> clusterspezifische Initialisierungsfunktionen: Benötigt ein Funktionscluster explizite Initialisierung oder Deinitialisierung, muss er ausschließlich <code>ara::core::Initialize</code>/<code>ara::core::Deinitialize</code> nutzen.</p>
<h4>Fehlerbehandlung, Nebenläufigkeit &amp; Einschränkungen</h4>
<p>Die Spezifikation definiert Thread-Safety präzise: Eine nicht-statische AUTOSAR-API-Memberfunktion ist thread-safe, wenn sie ohne Synchronisation durch den Aufrufer gleichzeitig auf demselben Objekt aus mehreren Threads aufgerufen werden darf; Destruktoren und Zuweisungsoperatoren sind üblicherweise nicht thread-safe <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13200">[SWS_CORE_13200]</a>. Wird eine nicht-thread-safe Memberfunktion dennoch konkurrierend auf demselben Objekt aufgerufen, ist das Verhalten undefiniert – selbst wenn die andere beteiligte Funktion thread-safe ist <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13203">[SWS_CORE_13203]</a>; ohne Synchronisation zulässig ist dagegen der konkurrierende Aufruf auf unterschiedlichen Instanzen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13205">[SWS_CORE_13205]</a>. Als non-thread-safe spezifizierte Callbacks bzw. rein virtuelle Funktionen ruft die ARA-Implementierung ausschließlich sequenziell auf, etwa <code>ara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseNotifier</code>, während z. B. <code>ara::phm::RecoveryAction::RecoveryHandler</code> thread-safe ist <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13214">[SWS_CORE_13214]</a>. Die Nutzung beliebiger ARA-APIs innerhalb eines Signal-Handlers führt zu undefiniertem Verhalten, sofern nicht anders spezifiziert <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13210">[SWS_CORE_13210]</a> (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>: Async-Signal-Safety). Zusätzlich verlangt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a>, dass jede API-Funktion ihren Thread-Safety-Level als „thread-safe“, „not thread-safe“ oder „conditional“ angibt, und dass der Thread-Safety-Vertrag bidirektional gilt: Ist eine API thread-safe spezifiziert, muss auch die vom Vendor oder Nutzer bereitgestellte Implementierung, etwa Callbacks oder rein virtuelle Skeleton-Funktionen, diese Zusage einhalten (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>).</p>
<p>Für nicht behebbare Fehler unterscheidet <code>ara::core</code> die Violation von der regulären Fehlerbehandlung: Eine Violation ist die Folge verletzter Vor- oder Nachbedingungen des Frameworks und nicht behebbar, vergleichbar einer fehlgeschlagenen Assertion <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a>. Bei einer standardisierten Violation wird der Prozess über <code>ara::core::Abort</code> abnormal beendet; eine Debug-Meldung gemäß der DLT-Definition wird auf <code>stderr</code> ausgegeben und soll mit der Context ID des erkennenden Funktionsclusters in die Log-Sinks geschrieben werden <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00090">[SWS_CORE_00090]</a>. Während ein Aufruf von <code>Abort</code> läuft, blockieren weitere Aufrufe die aufrufenden Threads <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12407">[SWS_CORE_12407]</a>; installierte Abort-Handler werden dabei in umgekehrter Installationsreihenfolge aufgerufen, ohne Handler wird <code>std::abort()</code> aufgerufen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12404">[SWS_CORE_12404]</a>. Diese Trennung von über <code>Result</code>/<code>ErrorCode</code> behebbaren Fehlern und nicht behebbaren Violations <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a> wird von der <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a> als genereller Grundsatz für alle AP-Funktionscluster gestützt.</p>
<h4>Integration &amp; Konfiguration</h4>
<p>Jeder ARA-Funktionscluster nutzt beim Logging über <code>ara::log</code> die standardisierten Log-and-Trace-Einstellungen aus <code>ara::core</code>, insbesondere Context ID und Message-ID-Bereich <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00055">[SWS_CORE_00055]</a>. Dazu definiert die Spezifikation standardisierte Log-Kontext-IDs je Funktionscluster, u. a. <code>#COM</code> für com, <code>#COR</code> für core, <code>#CRY</code> für crypto, <code>#DIA</code> für diag, <code>#EXE</code> für exec, <code>#LOG</code> für log und <code>#PER</code> für per <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90024">[SWS_CORE_90024]</a>. Auf Anforderungsebene ergänzt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a>, dass ARA-Interfaces <code>ara::core</code>-Typen anstelle der C++-Standardtypen verwenden müssen, sofern <code>ara::core</code> einen äquivalenten Typ bereitstellt. Da der Namespace <code>ara</code> vollständig für AUTOSAR reserviert ist, stehen alle Datentypen eines Funktionsclusters zusätzlich über eine Forwarding-Header-Datei <code>&lt;fc&gt;_fwd.h</code> zur Verfügung (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>).</p>
<h4>Quellen</h4>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#page=60">AUTOSAR AP SWS Core (R25-11)</a> – Software-Spezifikation des Moduls Core inklusive Initialisierung, Threading- und Fehlerregeln.</li>
<li><a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">AUTOSAR AP EXP InterfacesGuidelines (R25-11)</a> – Startup/Shutdown-Vertrag, Fehlerbehandlungskonzept, Thread- und Signal-Safety-Grundsätze.</li>
<li><a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General (R25-11)</a> – Anforderungen zu Initialisierung, Thread-Safety-Dokumentation, Fehlerklassifikation und Typverwendung.</li>
</ul><h4>Architekturkontext: gemeinsame Vertrags- und Laufzeittypen</h4><p>Die Core Types bündeln gemeinsame Klassen und Funktionalität für die öffentlichen Schnittstellen mehrerer Functional Clusters. <code>Result</code> und <code>Future</code> tragen rückgewinnbare Fehler als Rückgabewert, während <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> den gemeinsamen ARA-Lebenszyklus einordnen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.1">EXP PlatformDesign §18.1 „Error Handling“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.1.2">RS General §4.1.2 „Error handling“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.4">EXP PlatformDesign §18.4 „Global initialization and shutdown functions“</a></p><p>Die in <code>ara::core</code> bereitgestellten Container und View-Typen adressieren zudem die für Automotive-Anwendungen ungeeignete Speicherallokation mancher Standardbibliothekstypen; <code>StringView</code>, <code>Span</code>, <code>Optional</code> und <code>Variant</code> unterstützen außerdem Manifest-bezogene API-Konstrukte. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.2">EXP PlatformDesign §18.2 „Advanced data types“</a></p><h4>Kapitel-7-Vertrag zwischen Anwendung und Functional Clustern</h4><p>Core definiert den gemeinsamen Rahmen für alle Functional Clusters: <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> können weitere Cluster nach Implementierungsbedarf initialisieren bzw. deinitialisieren; Result-, Future- und ErrorDomain-Typen machen den Fehlervertrag in öffentlichen APIs wiederverwendbar. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=section.5.3">SWS Core §5.3 – Functional Cluster initialization</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.7">SWS Core §7.1.7 „Initialization/De-initialization“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS Core §7.2 „Error handling“</a></p><div class="diagram" id="diag-01"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewbox="0.00 0.00 562.00 71.00" style="max-width:749px">

</div><p class="diagram-note">Kollaborationsdiagramm: Die Anwendung nutzt Core als gemeinsamen Lebenszyklus- und Typvertrag; die Initialisierung weiterer Functional Clusters erfolgt implementierungsabhängig. <em>Teilweise Interpretation:</em> Die Zusammenfassung der Clusterbeziehung in einem Knoten abstrahiert einzelne Cluster-spezifische Startpfade. Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=section.5.3">SWS Core §5.3 – Functional Cluster initialization</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.7">SWS Core §7.1.7 „Initialization/De-initialization“</a>.</p><h4>Bindung modellierter Datentypen</h4><p>Für modellierte Implementierungsdatentypen definiert die Sprachbindung die C++-Abbildung; die Platform-Types-Spezifikation ordnet primitive Datentypen ebenfalls C++-Typen zu. <code>ara::core</code>-Typen bilden dabei den gemeinsamen Bibliotheksrahmen, auf den die generierten C++-APIs aufsetzen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LanguageBindingForModeledAPdatatypes.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS LanguageBinding §7.1 „C++ binding for CppImplementationDataTypes“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformTypes.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS PlatformTypes §7.1 „Primitive ImplementationDataTypes and their mapping to C++ datatypes“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS Core §7.4 „Core data types“</a></p></div>
